cost_note: cost_usd = approximate compute/bandwidth monthly cost for the app tier (database excluded) per scale tier (<1k, 1k-10k, 10k-100k, 100k-1M, 1M-10M, >10M DAU). Compliance flags reflect vendors' published programmes on the curation date; verify before signing.

items.name: Vercel
items.summary: Frontend cloud: global CDN, SSR and serverless/edge functions; made by the Next.js team.
items.static_residency_note: Vercel caches a static site's files on its CDN worldwide, with no region to pin them to, and may move data to the US and wherever its providers work; a data-residency rule is treated as not met for a static site

compliance.hipaa_note: BAA only on paid plans (add-on / Enterprise); verify
compliance.maturity_note: SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS; HIPAA BAA only on paid plans; audit logs and dedicated (Secure Compute) networking are Enterprise features; no HITRUST or FedRAMP.

strengths.text: Zero-config Next.js deploys, preview URLs per pull request
Zero-config deploys for most frontend frameworks, preview URLs per pull request

strengths: Global edge network gives fast TTFB everywhere
weaknesses: Hobby tier is non-commercial; bandwidth/function overages get expensive at scale
WebSockets on Functions are in public beta: a connection pins to one instance, so fan-out needs a shared pub/sub

items.name: Netlify
items.summary: Jamstack platform: CDN hosting, serverless/edge functions, forms, deploy previews.
items.static_residency_note: Netlify serves a static site's files from its global edge and keeps hosting, storage and logs with US providers; a function region moves only where functions run (and their durable cache), so only a US residency rule is met for a static site

compliance.maturity_note: SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and a PCI DSS v4.0 Report on Compliance; a BAA only on Enterprise plans (treated as not eligible); audit log on Enterprise plans only.

strengths: Excellent for static/content sites (Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit)
Built-in forms, redirects, split testing
weaknesses: Paid plans bill in credits (Personal $9/month with 1,000 credits, Pro $20/month for unlimited members with 3,000, no per-seat charge) spent on deploys, bandwidth and requests, so the bill follows usage once the credits run out

weaknesses.text: Function regions are limited (no India region by default)

weaknesses: No long-running servers
items.static_cost_note: Free plan covers a static site up to its monthly bandwidth/credit allowance

items.name: Cloudflare Pages + Workers
items.summary: Edge platform: static hosting with unmetered bandwidth, Workers (V8 isolates) at 300+ locations, Durable Objects for stateful/WebSocket workloads.

compliance.hipaa_note: BAA only under Enterprise agreements; treated as not eligible
compliance.maturity_note: Broad programme (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, FedRAMP for some services) but a BAA only under Enterprise agreements.

strengths: Static assets with no bandwidth charges: cheapest way to serve high-traffic content

strengths.text: Edge compute close to users everywhere, including Indian PoPs
Edge compute close to users everywhere

strengths: Durable Objects give WebSockets/stateful coordination at the edge
weaknesses: Workers runtime is not full Node.js (some npm packages need polyfills)

weaknesses.text: Next.js needs the OpenNext adapter; not every feature is supported

items.static_cost_note: Pages: static sites are free with unlimited bandwidth (500 builds/month on the free plan)
items.residency_note: Keeping data and TLS termination inside India or the EU needs the Data Localization Suite, an Enterprise add-on; treated as not meeting a residency rule.

items.name: Render
items.summary: Heroku-style PaaS: web services, workers, cron, managed Postgres and Key Value, deploy from Git or Docker.
items.static_residency_note: Render serves static sites from a global CDN and offers no region for them, so a data-residency rule is treated as not met for a static site

compliance.hipaa_note: HIPAA-enabled workspaces need the Scale plan ($499/month) or Enterprise, plus a 20% surcharge on usage
compliance.maturity_note: SOC 2 Type 2; HIPAA-enabled workspaces on higher tiers; no PCI attestation or single-tenant option.

strengths: Git-push deploys for any backend (Django, Rails, Node, Go, Docker)
Managed Postgres/Key Value alongside services
weaknesses: Fewer knobs than AWS/GCP at very large scale
items.local_file_disk_note: free instances have an ephemeral filesystem; a persistent disk attaches only to a paid instance (from $7/month) and is billed per GB

items.name: Railway
items.summary: Usage-billed PaaS with one-click databases and a visual project canvas.

compliance.maturity_note: SOC 2 only; no BAA, no PCI attestation, no dedicated tenancy.

strengths: Fastest path from repo to running app + database
Pay per resource used
weaknesses: Younger platform; fewer compliance attestations

items.name: Fly.io
items.summary: Runs Docker images as Firecracker micro-VMs close to users in many regions, with Anycast networking.

compliance.hipaa_note: HIPAA package at $99/month on any paid plan, with the BAA pre-signed (fly.io/pricing)
compliance.maturity_note: SOC 2 Type 2 and a BAA via a compliance add-on; no PCI attestation; isolation is per-VM, not per-tenant hardware.

strengths: Multi-region deploys with one command; great for realtime/websockets

weaknesses.text: No India region (Singapore is closest); the region list has none in India

weaknesses: More hands-on than Render/Railway
No free plan for new organizations (a trial of 2 machine-hours or 7 days); the smallest always-on machine costs about $2.19 a month

items.name: AWS ECS on Fargate
items.summary: Serverless containers on AWS: no nodes to manage, integrates with ALB, RDS, IAM, CloudWatch.

compliance.maturity_note: AWS: HIPAA-eligible services list, PCI DSS Level 1 service provider, HITRUST CSF and FedRAMP High; CloudTrail records every API call; Dedicated Hosts/Instances give single-tenant hardware; reports via AWS Artifact.

strengths: Containers without Kubernetes complexity
weaknesses: AWS networking/IAM learning curve
ALB + NAT gateway base costs even when idle

sla.scope: tasks spread over two or more Availability Zones (Amazon ECS / Fargate multi-AZ commitment)

items.name: AWS EKS (Kubernetes)
items.summary: Managed Kubernetes control plane on AWS.

compliance.maturity_note: AWS: HIPAA-eligible services list, PCI DSS Level 1 service provider, HITRUST CSF and FedRAMP High; CloudTrail records every API call; Dedicated Hosts/Instances give single-tenant hardware; reports via AWS Artifact.

strengths: Portable Kubernetes workloads with the AWS ecosystem
Fine-grained autoscaling for many services
weaknesses: Control-plane fee (~$73/mo) plus nodes
Needs dedicated platform/DevOps skills

sla.scope: a Provisioned Control Plane (99.99%; the standard control plane is 99.95%) with worker nodes on EC2 across two or more Availability Zones (Amazon Compute region-level SLA, 99.99%: https://aws.amazon.com/compute/sla/)

items.name: AWS Lambda + API Gateway
items.summary: Event-driven functions with per-request billing; API Gateway or function URLs in front.

compliance.maturity_note: AWS: HIPAA-eligible services list, PCI DSS Level 1 service provider, HITRUST CSF and FedRAMP High; CloudTrail records every API call; Dedicated Hosts/Instances give single-tenant hardware; reports via AWS Artifact.

strengths: Scale-to-zero billing with a permanent free tier (1M requests/month)
weaknesses: Cold starts; 15-minute execution limit
Relational DB connections need RDS Proxy
Cost overtakes containers at sustained high RPS

items.name: AWS S3 + CloudFront (static)
items.summary: Pre-built pages in an S3 bucket served through the CloudFront CDN: files only, no server code.

compliance.maturity_note: AWS: S3 and CloudFront are on the HIPAA-eligible services list and in scope for PCI DSS Level 1 and SOC reports; CloudTrail records every API call; reports via AWS Artifact.

items.static_cost_note: CloudFront flat-rate plans: Free $0 (1M requests, 100 GB), Pro $15, Business $200, Premium $1,000 a month, with no overage charges; S3 storage for a site's files is cents a month.
strengths: Plain files in a bucket: the cheapest and most portable way to serve a static site on AWS

strengths.text: S3 buckets in Mumbai and Hyderabad; CloudFront edge locations in India

strengths: CloudFront flat-rate plans with no overage charges
weaknesses: Serves files only: no server rendering, API routes or functions
Manual setup: bucket policy with Origin Access Control, a TLS certificate and a cache invalidation on each deploy

weaknesses.text: Next.js must use static export (output: 'export'): no ISR, middleware or on-demand image optimisation

items.name: Firebase Hosting (static)
items.summary: Google's static hosting: pre-built pages cached at CDN edges worldwide, deployed with the Firebase CLI; files only, no server code.
items.static_residency_note: Firebase Hosting is a global service: its files sit at CDN edges worldwide and their location cannot be chosen, so a data-residency rule is treated as not met

compliance.maturity_note: ISO 27001 and SOC 1, 2 and 3 (every Firebase service); Google lists Firebase Hosting in scope for its ISO 27001, SOC 2 and PCI DSS audits; not among the products Google Cloud's HIPAA BAA covers.

items.static_cost_note: Spark (no-cost) plan: 10 GB stored and 360 MB a day of transfer; on the Blaze plan $0.026 per GB stored and $0.15 per GB transferred past those.
strengths: One command (firebase deploy) publishes the site with a free certificate on your custom domain
The Spark plan costs nothing up to 10 GB stored and 360 MB a day of transfer
weaknesses: Serves files only: no server rendering, API routes or functions
Transfer past the free 360 MB a day costs $0.15 per GB, more than a flat-rate CDN at high traffic
The location of the files cannot be chosen, so it meets no data-residency rule

sla.scope: Firebase Hosting (service credits are a share of fees paid)

items.name: Google Cloud Storage + Cloud CDN (static)
items.summary: Pre-built pages in a Cloud Storage bucket in your region, behind an external Application Load Balancer with Cloud CDN: files only, no server code.

compliance.maturity_note: Cloud Storage, Cloud CDN and Cloud Load Balancing are among the products Google Cloud's HIPAA BAA covers (do not cache PHI), and Google lists all three in scope for its ISO 27001, SOC 2 and PCI DSS audits; Cloud Audit Logs record admin activity.

items.static_cost_note: The load balancer that gives the bucket HTTPS on your domain costs $0.025 an hour (about $18 a month) with no traffic; Cloud CDN cache egress is $0.08 per GiB to North America and Europe ($0.09 in Asia Pacific) for the first 10 TiB.
strengths: The bucket sits in the region you choose (asia-south1 Mumbai, europe-west3 Frankfurt, us-central1 Iowa), so the files stay there
Covered by Google Cloud's HIPAA BAA, with a 99.95% Cloud CDN SLA
weaknesses: About $18 a month for the load balancer even with no traffic: Cloud Storage alone serves no HTTPS on a custom domain
Manual setup: bucket, backend bucket, load balancer, certificate and cache policy

sla.scope: Cloud Storage Standard class in one region (Cloud CDN: 99.95%)

items.name: Azure Static Web Apps
items.summary: Azure's static hosting: pre-built pages distributed globally, deployed from GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps; files only here, no server code.
items.static_residency_note: Static Web Apps is a global service: its files are distributed worldwide and the region you pick places only the managed Functions API, so a data-residency rule is treated as not met

compliance.maturity_note: No public page checked here states its HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 or ISO 27001 scope (Azure's audit-scope appendix is a Service Trust Portal document), so it is treated as holding none of them until checked.

items.static_cost_note: Free plan: 100 GB of bandwidth a month per subscription and 0.5 GB of storage, with no SLA (a site over its quota is not served); Standard plan: $9 per app a month, then $0.20 per GB past 100 GB.
strengths: The Free plan costs nothing for a small site, with free certificates on two custom domains
Builds and deploys from GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps on every push, with preview environments for pull requests
weaknesses: Serves files only here: no server rendering; its API is a separate managed Functions app
The Free plan has no SLA and stops serving a site that exceeds its quota
The files are distributed globally with no region to pin, so it meets no data-residency rule

sla.scope: Standard plan (the Free plan has none)

items.name: Azure Blob Storage + Front Door (static)
items.summary: Pre-built pages in a Blob Storage static website in your region, behind Azure Front Door Standard: files only, no server code.

compliance.maturity_note: Microsoft's Azure Storage page puts Blobs in Azure's ISO, SOC and PCI DSS audits, but no public Microsoft page lists Front Door's audit scope, and the services the HIPAA BAA covers are listed only in a Service Trust Portal document; so the pairing is treated as holding none of them until checked.

items.static_cost_note: Front Door Standard costs $35 a month plus $0.0825 per GB out to North America and Europe for the first 10 TB; Blob storage for a site's files is cents a month.
strengths: The storage account sits in the region you choose (Central India, Germany West Central, East US), so the files stay there
Front Door Standard carries a 99.99% SLA
weaknesses: $35 a month for Front Door even with no traffic; Azure CDN (classic) takes no new profiles and retires on 30 September 2027
Manual setup: storage account, static website, Front Door profile, custom domain and certificate

items.name: Google Cloud Run
items.summary: Serverless containers: any Docker image, request-based autoscaling to zero, WebSockets supported.

compliance.maturity_note: Google Cloud: BAA covering listed services, PCI DSS, HITRUST CSF, FedRAMP High; Cloud Audit Logs are on by default for admin activity; sole-tenant nodes give dedicated hardware.

strengths: Container portability with serverless billing
No cluster to operate
weaknesses: Request timeout (max 60 min) limits very long-lived connections
Cold starts when scaled to zero

sla.scope: Cloud Run services in most regions

scale_to_zero.why: Scales to zero by default; minimum instances avoid cold starts and are billed while idle

items.name: Google Kubernetes Engine (Autopilot)
items.summary: Managed Kubernetes; Autopilot mode manages nodes for you.

compliance.maturity_note: Google Cloud: BAA covering listed services, PCI DSS, HITRUST CSF, FedRAMP High; Cloud Audit Logs are on by default for admin activity; sole-tenant nodes give dedicated hardware.

strengths: Most mature managed Kubernetes; Autopilot reduces node ops
Good fit for many services / ML workloads with GPUs
weaknesses: Kubernetes expertise still required
Cluster management fee

sla.scope: Autopilot Pods in multiple zones (the control plane is 99.95%)

items.name: Azure App Service
items.summary: Microsoft's managed web hosting and serverless containers, integrated with Entra ID and Azure SQL/Postgres.

compliance.maturity_note: Azure: HIPAA BAA in the product terms, PCI DSS Level 1, HITRUST, FedRAMP High; Activity Log audits every control-plane change; Azure Dedicated Host gives single-tenant servers.

strengths: Natural home for .NET and Microsoft-centric enterprises
Broad compliance portfolio
weaknesses: Portal/config complexity; pricing tiers are confusing

sla.scope: App Service apps deployed across two or more Availability Zones (zone-redundant Premium v2-v4 plans); 99.95% without zones, and Azure Container Apps 99.95%

items.name: DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs)
items.summary: Developer-friendly cloud: App Platform PaaS, Droplets, managed Postgres/MySQL/Valkey, Bangalore region.

compliance.maturity_note: SOC 2 Type II; for PCI DSS it validates only SAQ-A (it keeps no card data itself), so it is not attested as a service provider for systems that store card data. DigitalOcean signs a HIPAA BAA only for listed products (Droplets, Kubernetes, Spaces, Volumes and others); App Platform and Managed Databases, which this option uses, are not on the list.

strengths: Predictable, low pricing

strengths.text: Bangalore (BLR1) region for Indian users / data residency

weaknesses: Fewer managed services than hyperscalers

weaknesses.text: Its HIPAA BAA does not cover App Platform or Managed Databases (only Droplets, Kubernetes and other listed products)
DigitalOcean lists static sites in BLR (Bangalore) as having limited availability, through the Cloudflare CDN only

items.static_cost_note: Three static-site apps are free with 1 GiB of transfer each a month; more transfer is $0.02 per GiB, and static-only apps past three are $3 a month each.

items.name: Hetzner Cloud / VPS (Docker, Coolify)
items.summary: Low-cost VMs in Germany, Finland, US and Singapore; you run Docker/Compose or a self-hosted PaaS like Coolify.

compliance.maturity_note: ISO 27001 data centres only; no SOC 2 report, BAA or PCI attestation.

strengths: 3-10x cheaper compute than hyperscalers
weaknesses: You own patching, backups, failover and monitoring

items.name: On-prem VMs + Docker Compose
items.summary: Your own servers or private data centre running containers with Compose/systemd and a reverse proxy.

compliance.maturity_note: Every control (audit logging, access review, encryption, physical security) is yours to build and evidence; a single Docker host has no built-in audit trail.

strengths: Full data control; simplest on-prem option for small teams
Easy to move to Kubernetes later (same images)
weaknesses: Manual scaling and failover
Hardware capex + sysadmin time
items.single_host_note: Docker Compose runs an app's containers on one Docker host and restarts them only on that host; placing and moving containers across several hosts is what Swarm or Kubernetes add

items.name: On-prem Kubernetes (k3s / RKE2 / OpenShift)
items.summary: Self-operated Kubernetes in your own data centre.

compliance.maturity_note: Every control is yours to evidence, but Kubernetes has built-in API audit logging and RBAC.

strengths: Data sovereignty + cloud-like orchestration
No per-request vendor bills
weaknesses: Requires a platform team (upgrades, storage, networking, security)
Capex and long hardware lead times
